seoTitle: Ibiza cruise port guide: Botafoc, Dalt Vila and buses
seoDescription: Big ships berth at Botafoc, 3 km across the bay from Dalt Vila. Walk 35–40 min or take the shuttle or City Boat. Town bus €1.70 by card (2026).
quickAnswer: Most cruise ships berth at the Botafoc breakwater, about 3 km across the harbour from Ibiza Town; some smaller ships tie up in the town harbour below the old walls. From Botafoc, take the PortBus shuttle, the City Boat water taxi or a 10–15 minute taxi, or walk 35–40 minutes round the bay. Be back at the shuttle or boat stop in town 90 minutes before all-aboard if you are in Dalt Vila.
intro: Ibiza Town is two places for a cruise passenger: La Marina, the flat harbour district, and Dalt Vila, the walled upper town above it, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999. Large ships berth at Botafoc on the far side of the bay, so the day starts with a short transfer. Dalt Vila is steep and cobbled, and the climb takes longer than the map suggests. Plan the walls and cathedral for the cooler morning, and keep the afternoon for La Marina or a beach.
tenderNotes: Tendering is uncommon but can happen when the port is busy. Ships normally berth.

terminals.name: Botafoc breakwater (Dique del Botafoc / Muelle Ribera Botafoc)
terminals.notes: Main berth for large and medium ships, across the harbour from the old town. The port authority map shows a provisional maritime station here, with a tourist information point. Taxis, shuttle buses and the City Boat stop at Marina Botafoc serve it.

terminals.name: Town harbour (Muelle de Levante area)
terminals.notes: Used by some smaller ships, near the base of the old town walls. Passengers step ashore in La Marina and can walk to Dalt Vila in 5–10 minutes.

walkability.detail: From Botafoc the walk round the bay to Ibiza Town takes about 35–40 minutes on the harbour road, with little shade. Add 15–20 minutes and a steep climb to reach the cathedral at the top of Dalt Vila. Ships berthed in the town harbour are a 5–10 minute walk from the gates.

transportSections.cost: Fare not confirmed; pay the driver
transportSections.detail: Runs between Botafoc and Ibiza Town during cruise calls, setting down near the marina below the old town. Many cruise lines also run their own shuttle to the same area; check your daily programme.

transportSections.cost: Fare not confirmed; tickets at the booth or on board
transportSections.detail: City Boat Ibiza links Ibiza Town (wooden ticket cabin at the port) with Marina Botafoc, with a stop for Talamanca beach, roughly every 30 minutes. Timetables change through the season.
Taxis wait outside the Botafoc terminal. Vehicles cannot enter Dalt Vila; drivers set down at Portal de ses Taules or near the Hotel Mirador at the top.
Follow the harbour road round the bay. Fine on a cool morning; tiring in July and August.

transportSections.cost: €1.70 by card or QR, €2.40 cash for an urban trip; €3.35 card / €4.70 cash to Ses Salines on line P3 (2026)
transportSections.detail: Alsa runs the island network from 2026. The main bus station, CETIS, is on the edge of town, about 15 minutes' walk from the harbour. Paying by card or in advance is cheaper than cash.

returnTiming.rule: With the ship at Botafoc, be at the shuttle or City Boat stop in Ibiza Town 75 minutes before all-aboard, and leave Dalt Vila 90 minutes before. If you walk back round the bay, leave town 105 minutes before.
returnTiming.detail: Everyone heads back at the same time, so shuttle and boat queues grow in the last two hours. The climb down from the cathedral through the lanes takes 15–20 minutes. If your ship is in the town harbour, 60 minutes on board before all-aboard is enough.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: Take a taxi from the rank in La Marina to Botafoc (10–15 minutes). If you will miss all-aboard, call the port agent number on your daily programme at once.

diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner
diyVsExcursion.diy: Free on your own; Ibiza Free Tours runs a free two-hour walk from Plaça Vara de Rey (book online)
diyVsExcursion.saving: Most of the ship tour price

diyVsExcursion.ship: Varies by line; check your cruise planner
diyVsExcursion.diy: Bus P3 €3.35 by card each way (2026), from CETIS

excursionAdvice: Skip the ship tour for Dalt Vila: the old town is compact, free to enter and easy to see alone, and a free guided walk exists. A ship tour is worth it for an island tour (Es Vedrà, Ses Salines, Santa Gertrudis) or the Cova de Can Marçà, which need a car and 4–5 hours. Take the ship's tour if you want Formentera: the ferry is only 30–40 minutes each way, but a delayed return sailing on your own means a missed ship.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship berths at Botafoc at 08:00 and all-aboard is 17:30.

steps.what: Off the ship. Take the shuttle or the City Boat across to Ibiza Town.
Enter Dalt Vila by Portal de ses Taules and climb through the lanes to the cathedral before the heat.
Walk the ramparts and bastions (30–45 minutes) for views over the harbour towards Formentera.
MACE contemporary art museum, free entry (closed Mondays).
Lunch near Plaça de Vila or down in La Marina.
Option A: City Boat to Talamanca beach. Option B: browse La Marina and the harbour front.
Be at the shuttle or City Boat stop in Ibiza Town (from Talamanca, walk to the Marina Botafoc side instead).
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Dalt Vila and its Renaissance walls
sights.why: The walled upper town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999; the 16th-century walls are almost complete.
sights.tip: Portal de ses Taules is the main and steepest way in; Portal Nou is gentler.

sights.name: Ibiza Cathedral (Santa Maria)
sights.why: Built on the site of a former mosque at the highest point of Dalt Vila, with wide views over the port.
sights.tip: Hours are seasonal; check on the day. Cover shoulders and knees, and avoid Sunday Mass at 10:30.

sights.name: Ramparts and bastions
sights.why: A walk along the walls past bastions such as Sant Joan and Santa Llúcia, with views to Formentera.
sights.tip: No shade at midday in summer.

sights.name: MACE (Museu d'Art Contemporani d'Eivissa)
sights.why: Contemporary art in an 18th-century military building inside the walls, with an archaeological site below.
sights.tip: October to March: Tuesday–Friday 10:00–16:30, weekends 10:00–14:00. April to September: Tuesday–Sunday 10:00–14:00 plus Tuesday–Friday evenings. Closed Mondays and holidays.

sights.name: Museu Puget and Casa Broner
sights.why: Two small free municipal museums: a painter's house in Dalt Vila and an architect's house in Sa Penya.

sights.name: Puig des Molins necropolis and museum
sights.why: A Phoenician–Punic burial ground from the 7th century BC with thousands of tombs, just outside the old town.
sights.tip: The Dalt Vila archaeological museum is closed for works, so this is the place to see the island's ancient finds.

sights.name: La Marina
sights.why: The flat harbour district below the walls: shops, cafés and the waterfront.
sights.tip: Good for the last hour before the shuttle, as it is next to the boat and shuttle stops.

beaches.name: Talamanca
beaches.howToGetThere: Short walk from the Botafoc side, or the City Boat stop
beaches.time: A few minutes from Marina Botafoc
beaches.note: Shallow water and restaurants along a boardwalk. The closest beach to the cruise berth.

beaches.name: Figueretes
beaches.howToGetThere: Walk south from the town centre

beaches.name: Platja d'en Bossa
beaches.howToGetThere: City Boat from Ibiza Town (about hourly) or taxi
beaches.note: Ibiza's longest beach and the centre of the beach club scene; 3 km south of town.

beaches.name: Ses Salines
beaches.howToGetThere: Alsa bus P3 from CETIS bus station
beaches.note: Only on a long call, given the walk to CETIS and the bus timetable.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming the ship docks in town.
commonMistakes.fix: Large ships berth at Botafoc, 3 km away. Plan the shuttle or boat both ways.

commonMistakes.mistake: Climbing Dalt Vila at midday in July or August.
commonMistakes.fix: Go up first thing and do La Marina or a beach in the afternoon.
Card or QR fares are cheaper: €1.70 instead of €2.40 in town (2026).

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning to see the archaeological museum in Dalt Vila.
commonMistakes.fix: It is closed for works; go to Puig des Molins instead.

commonMistakes.mistake: Doing Formentera on your own on a short call.
commonMistakes.fix: A delayed return ferry means a missed ship. Use the ship's tour or stay on Ibiza.

safety: Ibiza Town is safe by day for cruise visitors. The UK government warns that thieves in Spain use distraction techniques and often work in teams, so keep bags closed in crowded lanes and on the shuttle. The Dalt Vila lanes are steep, cobbled and slippery; wear shoes with grip. At beaches, a red flag means you must not enter the water, and some spots have strong undercurrents. San Antonio, not Ibiza Town, has the strict alcohol rules for party areas.
scams: Distraction theft: thieves work in teams and distract you while one takes a wallet or phone. Keep valuables split up and bags closed.
Fake police: people posing as plain-clothes officers ask to see your wallet. Real police may ask for ID but never for your wallet or purse.
Timeshare and holiday club offers: the UK government warns some are fraudulent and use false incentives. Do not sign anything on the street.
accessibility: La Marina and the harbour front are flat. Dalt Vila is steep and cobbled, with steps near the cathedral square, and vehicles cannot enter the walls; there is no practical step-free route to the cathedral. A tunnel next to the Hotel Mirador gives access near the top, and taxis can set down there, so some visitors ride up and walk down. Portal Nou is less steep than Portal de ses Taules. Ask your ship whether its shuttle is accessible.
rainyDay: Use the free municipal museums: the MACE, Museu Puget and Casa Broner, which share opening hours and close on Mondays. Puig des Molins has an indoor museum as well as the necropolis. Take care on the wet stone lanes in Dalt Vila.
crowdTips: Shuttle and boat queues are longest just after the ship opens its gangway and in the last two hours of the call; wait 20 minutes in the morning or come back early. July and August are the busiest and hottest months; April–May and September–October are calmer.

faqs.q: Where do cruise ships dock in Ibiza?
faqs.a: Most berth at the Botafoc breakwater, about 3 km across the harbour from Ibiza Town. Some smaller ships use the town harbour below Dalt Vila.

faqs.q: Is Ibiza walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Partly. From Botafoc it is a 35–40 minute walk round the bay to Ibiza Town, then a steep climb into Dalt Vila. From the town harbour, Dalt Vila is 5–10 minutes away.

faqs.q: How do I get from Ibiza cruise port to Dalt Vila?
faqs.a: Take the PortBus or ship's shuttle, the City Boat water taxi or a 10–15 minute taxi into town, then walk up through Portal de ses Taules.
Rarely. Ships normally berth, though tendering can happen when the port is busy.

faqs.q: What can I do in Ibiza in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Dalt Vila, the cathedral and the walls in the morning, a free museum, lunch, then Talamanca beach or La Marina.
Talamanca is a few minutes from Marina Botafoc. Figueretes is at the south edge of town and Platja d'en Bossa is 3 km south.

faqs.q: How much is the bus in Ibiza?
faqs.a: An urban trip on the Alsa network costs €1.70 by card or QR or €2.40 in cash (2026).
Yes for a day visit. Watch for pickpockets in crowds and take care on the steep cobbles.
